description: Issue #178, the fail-closed half — the same rule the `acceptance-gates` block already follows (acceptance-gates-notation.md section 7): a broken `open-questions` block is NEVER rounded to 'there was no block'. Four ways to break it — two blocks in one body, a version this runner does not implement, a key the v1 block does not define, and a block that asks nothing — each raise `open_question_block_invalid` as an open question and drop the run to `partial`, so dispatch refuses the issue. Rounding a broken block to an absent one is how a run ends green with the author's declared undecidables silently gone, which is the exact failure this notation exists to prevent.

warning_details_include: #440: The `open-questions` block could not be read: the body carries 2 blocks and exactly one is allowed
#441: The `open-questions` block could not be read: version must be exactly 1 (got "2")
#442: The `open-questions` block could not be read: unknown key "answers"
#443: The `open-questions` block could not be read: the block asks nothing
It is NOT treated as absent
The planner never reads an open question out of prose.
The dispatch runner refuses an issue with an unanswered question
